__comment: GLOBAL abbreviation map, shared by every paper in the pipeline. An entry earns its place two ways only: (a) a paper DEFINES it in its own text as 'Full name (ABBR)', recorded with that paper's DOI in `source`; or (b) it is one of a handful of universally-used ones, recorded as source 'common'. Nothing else. An abbreviation that is not here does not resolve, and rows using it stay out of the graph.
__workflow: Adding a paper: run --steps text, then --steps aliases, review data/alias_candidates.csv, and paste in the rows you believe. Then re-run --steps text for EVERY paper -- that is free, because the model responses are cached -- and reload the graph. Earlier papers get re-assessed against the growing map.
__warning: Do NOT fill these in from general chemistry knowledge, and do NOT trust the LLM's expansion. Asked to expand this paper's abbreviations, qwen3 got roughly half wrong, and its wrong answers were real chemicals that exist in Table 2 -- so nothing downstream would catch them. In THIS paper Gly is glycolic acid (not glycerol) and AA is acetamide (not acetic acid); both were established by matching a prose value against a Table 2 row, not by recall.
__values: `name` should be a component name that Table 2 uses; it is redirected to Table 2's most frequent spelling automatically. A record whose `name` is null is DELIBERATELY unresolved -- see LA.

ChAc.name: Choline acetate
ChAc.evidence: The melting point of choline acetate (ChAc)-based DESs follows the order

TEAB.name: Tetraethylammnoium bromide
TEAB.evidence: the melting point of Tetraethylammnoium bromide(TEAB)-based DESs
TEAB.note: Table 2 spells this two ways -- the paper's own typo has 8 rows, the correct spelling 3. This points at the typo so prose merges with the busier node. Fix by cleaning the table, not by editing this line.

MTPB.name: methyltriphenylphosphnium bromide
MTPB.note: not a Table 2 component, so this creates its own prose-only Component node

Py.name: Pyrogallol
Py.note: lookup is case-insensitive, so this also covers the paper's 'PY'

LA.ambiguous: This paper uses LA for BOTH acids. It defines 'ChCl:Lactic acid (LA)' inline, but the density section's 'TBAB:LA (1:4, 1.1031)' is unambiguously Table 2 row T2-0625, Tetrabutylammonium bromide:Levulinic acid -- and Table 2 has zero TBAB+Lactic acid rows. A null name keeps both readings out of the graph.
